title: Final pressure at room temperature
description: Essential: The student must state the correct numerical pressure after injection, approximately 3.2 × 10⁷ Pa.

title: Final pressure at high temperature
description: Essential: The student must state the correct numerical pressure after heating, approximately 1.6 × 10⁸ Pa.

title: Correct gas transfer model
description: Important: The student must correctly model the gas transfer using the ideal gas law, accounting for the gas remaining in the bottles.

title: Effective transferred volume
description: Important: The student must calculate the volume of gas transferred from each bottle based on the pressure drop and bottle volume.

title: Temperature conversion and use
description: Important: The student must correctly convert Celsius temperatures to Kelvin for use in the ideal gas law.

title: Application of Gay-Lussac's law
description: Optional: The student may explicitly state or correctly apply Gay-Lussac's law (p/T constant at constant volume) for the heating stage.

title: Unit consistency check
description: Optional: The student demonstrates consistent use of SI units (m³, Pa, K) throughout the calculation.

title: Incorrect temperature scaling
description: Pitfall: The student incorrectly uses Celsius instead of Kelvin in the ideal gas law for the heating calculation.

title: Ignoring bottle residual pressure
description: Pitfall: The student assumes all gas from the bottles is transferred, ignoring the final pressure in the bottles.
